public_rationale: The financial clause is checkable, and contemporary reports are consistent with its broad description: OpenAI projected roughly $5 billion of losses, while Anthropic reportedly burned $5.6 billion. But the combined claim also says the companies 'do not appear' to have found a way to stop. That is a qualified appraisal without a stated test. Anthropic's reported 2027 forecast is relevant, and Zitron acknowledged it. Its existence does not automatically refute his doubt; its uncertainty does not establish that doubt as fact. Scoring the entire statement would require replacing his qualification with an evaluator's threshold.
limitations: This is not a finding that the numerical financial clause is false.
The cited contemporary reports distinguish projected losses from reported cash burn.
News reporting is used because the underlying contemporary financial documents were not available in the readable sources.
No forecast of permanent losses or future failure is attributed to the speaker.

our_interpretation: The numerical clause is a checkable historical observation. I read 'billions' as at least $2 billion annually for each company separately.
I use calendar 2024, the latest completed annual period before publication, for the numerical clause. The surrounding discussion explicitly concerns 2024 figures.
The context uses 'burning' broadly for financial losses, including noncash costs. It does not consistently mean cash burn as measured in a cash-flow statement.

The second clause expresses a qualified impression as of February 17, 2025. It does not assert that neither company has a plan, that neither can become profitable, or that losses will continue until a particular deadline.

The speaker supplies no objective threshold for 'appear to have found a way'. Requiring a demonstrated sustainable route would strengthen his words. Treating a management forecast as automatically refuting them would also remove the qualification.
Because the supplied claim combines a checkable financial observation with that unscorable appraisal, I do not assign a binary verdict to the whole statement.
criteria.support_condition: The financial clause would be supported by appropriately defined 2024 figures showing at least $2 billion of annual losses or burn for each company, retaining the distinction between those measures. There is no speaker-supplied observable condition that conclusively establishes the qualified appraisal; supporting the financial clause alone does not settle the combined statement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The financial clause would be contradicted by comparable 2024 figures below $2 billion for either company under the intended measure. The existence of a plan or forecast alone does not contradict 'do not appear'. A definitive contradiction condition for that appraisal would require adding a threshold the speaker did not supply.

The reported 2024 burn is consistent with the numerical description for Anthropic. The same sentence records a planned reduction; neither fact decides whether a way to stop burning money appeared to have been found.
